title: Threat Research Engineer

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. /p p The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. /em /p /div div id= message-list_1790846969.120739 div div div div div div div div div div div An overview of this role /div div br As an Threat Research Engineer at GitLab, you'll research emerging security threats and turn your findings into protection for GitLab customers. You'll investigate new attack surfaces, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems, and build systems that help detect threats and improve vulnerability advisories. br This is a full-stack role: you'll take an idea from the first research question to a working proof of concept, deploy it, and analyze the results yourself. Artificial intelligence (AI) is central to how we work. You'll use AI tools daily and build agentic workflows for research, analysis, and detection. br br What you'll do /div ul li Research new attack surfaces and threat vectors, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems. /li li Find and responsibly disclose vulnerabilities in open source projects and developer tools. /li li Analyze software supply chain incidents and events. /li li Build AI-powered workflows and agents that automate research, analysis, and detection. /li li Build and maintain the cloud-based systems behind our detection and advisory work. /li li Improve the quality and coverage of our vulnerability and malware advisories. /li li Write up your findings as blog posts and present them at conferences. /li /ul div What you'll bring /div ul li Hands-on security experience in research, malware analysis, penetration testing, or security tooling, with an understanding of package ecosystems and software supply chain attacks. /li li Both a developer mindset and an adversarial mindset: you can build systems and think about how to break them. /li li Demonstrated experience using AI in real work, such as building with large language model (LLM) application programming interfaces (APIs) or agent frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or agent software development kits (SDKs). /li li Strong programming skills in Go or Python, with good software engineering practices, including testing, code review, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), and writing maintainable code. /li li Experience deploying and running production services on a public cloud. /li li The ability to map attack vectors, explain trade-offs, and use data to move experiments forward, balancing quality, speed, and customer outcomes. /li li Clear writing for engineers and a general audience, and keeping up with security and AI industry trends. /li li Helpful, but not required: Google Cloud Platform (GCP); Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) entries or published findings; research on AI agents, LLM applications, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers; blogs, talks, or open source security tools; Terraform or OpenTofu; databases or data pipelines at scale; reverse engineering. /li li You don't need deep knowledge of compilers or static application security testing (SAST) engines. A high-level understanding is enough. /li /ul div About the team br We're the Threat Research group. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. /em /p /div h2 An overview of this role /h2 p Help us build the next generation of authentication services at GitLab. As a Senior Backend Engineer on the Authentication team, you'll build authentication features across the Rails monolith and GATE. GATE is our new service for issuing and validating tokens and managing identities, designed to support every GitLab deployment model. /p p You'll expand authentication mechanisms, including support for identities used by artificial intelligence (AI) agents. You'll also help keep GitLab and its customers secure by building access management tooling and addressing vulnerabilities reported through our HackerOne program. /p p GATE will become the foundation for token issuance, validation, and identity services across GitLab.com multi-tenant software as a service (SaaS), Self-Managed, Dedicated, and air-gapped environments. Your work will affect core components that customers, users, and GitLab teams rely on. /p p Some of our projects include: /p ul li value= 1 Building GATE as the centralized service for token issuance and validation /li li value= 2 Consolidating tokens and migrating authentication paths out of the Rails monolith /li li value= 3 Building passkeys and passwordless authentication /li li value= 4 Developing composite identities that combine machine and human authorization for AI /li li value= 5 Improving service accounts and secure automation /li li value= 6 Enhancing Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML), Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP), OpenID Connect (OIDC), and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) capabilities for automated user provisioning and single sign-on (SSO) /li /ul h2 What you'll do /h2 ul li value= 1 Shape the roadmap for GATE and GitLab's authentication services with the team. /li li value= 2 Design and implement token issuance, validation, and identity services in Go and Ruby across the Rails monolith and GATE, including new authentication mechanisms such as Workload Identity Federation. /li li value= 3 Migrate authentication and token management paths from the monolith into GATE while maintaining reliability across all deployment models. /li li value= 4 Build authentication mechanisms from the ground up, such as Workload Identity Federation. /li li value= 5 Strengthen security for users and organizations through access management tooling and by addressing vulnerabilities reported through our HackerOne program. /li li value= 6 Define and improve standards for style, maintainability, and engineering practices in a high-scale environment, and advocate for them through code review. /li li value= 7 Communicate publicly about GitLab initiatives, projects, and contributions from people not working for GitLab Inc. Reflect GitLab's values in these communications. /li li value= 8 Ship moderately sized features and improvements with moderate guidance and support from other team members, and collaborate on larger projects, including the build-out of GATE. /li li value= 9 Participate in the maintainer trainee program at your own comfortable pace while working toward becoming a project maintainer. /li /ul h2 What you'll bring /h2 ul li value= 1 Professional experience with Go and/or Ruby in scaling or mission-critical SaaS products. /li li value= 2 Familiarity with authentication and authorization technologies or techniques, such as OAuth, OIDC, SAML, SSO, SCIM, LDAP, JSON Web Tokens (JWTs), role-based access control (RBAC), or identity and access management (IAM). /li li value= 3 Knowledge of token systems, cryptographic signing, and key management. /li li value= 4 Experience building or contributing to a service from concept to production, including proposal, discussion, and execution. /li li value= 5 Proficiency in written and verbal English, with the ability to communicate complex problems and solutions clearly in a remote, largely asynchronous work environment. /li li value= 6 Experience diagnosing, preventing, and resolving performance and optimization problems. /li li value= 7 Experience working in an iterative software development process, managing your work effectively, staying organized, and following through on priorities. /li /ul h2 About the team /h2 p Our mission is to empower GitLab system administrators with the toolkit they need to create their desired balance of security and accessibility for their GitLab experience. /p p Authentication is the first impression a new customer has when they configure a new GitLab instance.
